reason: Entries: .cell only by fall-through from .cells_on_page and the window's own BCC/BRA; .byte/.last_cell/.part_byte only from inside the window; no label+N references. The record's byte 10 (s_ptr+1 at .more) is written only by draw_column (line 1742) from s_ptr+1 = b_ptr+1 or its up_cell result, all kept in &40-&7F (raise_address, forward/back/flipped ring wraps, up_cell CMP/ADC #&40); subsequent cells come from this same next-cell step. From &40-&7F, SBC #&02 with C 0 or 1 gives &3D-&7E, for which ORA #&40 alone equals AND #&3F/ORA #&40 (&3D-&3F -> &7D-&7F, &40-&7E unchanged). draw_column's next-cell code (line 1799-1801) already uses ORA #&40 alone, so the restore walk now mirrors the draw exactly. AND does not touch C or V; ORA sets N/Z from the identical result, and LDA v_ptr overwrites them anyway; C (needed by ADC #7) comes from SBC #&02 unchanged. No register, stack or memory change; IRQ sees nothing different (s_ptr+1 written with the same value by the same STA). SKIP 2 after the unconditional JMP columns is never executed and keeps .compiled and everything after at the same address. Saves 2 cycles (AND #imm) per next cell, 0 bytes net.
